newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes higher; Oman market very strong.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes higher; Oman market very strong.

text.p: Cash crude prices were firm in Asia on Thursday with Oman taking the spotlight as the crude started trading March at firm premiums.
A Japanese trader paid MPM plus 29 cents for a cargo of March Oman from a European major, possibly spurred on by Wednesday's talk of China buying at plus 31 cents.
China came back into market discussion on Thursday and was heard paying plus 32 cents to a trader for a March cargo, reiterating China's strong buying presence.
The Oman market was seeing offers above 30 cents and bids between 25 and 30 cents in late afternoon, traders said.
The premium levels for Oman surprised even sellers. They said they had expected a firm level for Oman in March, but not necessarily at such an early stage of trading.
The Oman/Dubai differential for March widened to $1.04 from 86 cents and Oman in February went out at MPM plus 30 cents, indicating March premiums were very strong.
Elsewhere, Middle East trading was quiet with little discussion of premium levels.
A European major sold a late 550,000 barrels of February Lower Zakum at ADNOC plus 60 cents, down 20-25 cents from the last February deals.

The Cossack and Griffin shut downs continued to play on sentiment. Sources said shipping delays were around nine days and some refiners in Australia were looking for fill-in barrels and altering output schedules.
A U.S. major was heard seeking an Indonesia-Australia east coast charter to lift fill in barrels, sources said.
The sentiment underpinned Tapis paper, which rose 20 cents.
January was quoted at $25.70/$26.05 and February at $25.50/$25.60.
